title: In the gullet
stem: Which of the following happens in the gullet?
key: The gullet only moves food along. Its muscles squeeze in waves and push the food down to the stomach.

options.text: Water is absorbed from the food.
options.pick: You may remember that water is absorbed somewhere in the digestive system.
options.why: Water is absorbed from undigested food in the large intestine. The food in the gullet is still on its way down.

options.text: Digestive juices break the food down into tiny pieces.
options.pick: The gullet is part of the digestive system, so it feels as if it must digest food.
options.why: No digestive juice is made in the gullet. Saliva from the mouth is mixed with the food, but the gullet's job is to move the food along.

options.text: Muscles in its wall squeeze the food down to the stomach.
options.pick: Think about what the gullet is: a muscular tube joining the mouth to the stomach.
options.why: The gullet is a muscular tube. Its muscles squeeze in waves behind the food and push it down to the stomach.

options.text: Digested food is absorbed into the blood.
options.pick: Absorption sounds like something that happens soon after food is swallowed.
options.why: The food has not been digested yet in the gullet. Digested food is absorbed into the blood in the small intestine.

title: In the stomach
stem: Which of the following happens in the stomach?
key: The stomach churns the food and gastric juice partly digests it. Digestion is not finished here.

options.text: Muscles churn the food while gastric juice turns it into a thick liquid.
options.pick: The stomach has a strong muscular wall and makes gastric juice. What do those two do to the food?
options.why: The stomach wall is muscular. It churns the food and mixes it with gastric juice, which digests the food into a thick liquid.

options.text: Teeth cut the food into small pieces.
options.pick: Cutting food up is the first step, and the stomach is where the food ends up.
options.why: Teeth are in the mouth. The stomach has muscles that churn the food, not teeth.

options.text: All the food is completely digested and absorbed into the blood.
options.pick: The stomach is the biggest bag in the system, so it seems to do the whole job.
options.why: In the stomach the food is only partly digested. Digestion is completed, and the digested food is absorbed, in the small intestine.

options.text: Water is absorbed from the undigested food.
options.pick: Water absorption is a well-known job of the digestive system.
options.why: Water is absorbed from undigested food in the large intestine, not in the stomach.

title: Completely digested food
stem: Which of the following happens to completely digested food?
key: Completely digested food passes into the blood in the small intestine. Only undigested food moves on.

options.text: Water is absorbed from it.
options.pick: Water absorption is a well-known job of the digestive system.
options.why: Water is absorbed from undigested food in the large intestine. Completely digested food has already been absorbed into the blood.

options.text: It is absorbed into the blood at the small intestine.
options.pick: Completely digested food is in tiny pieces that dissolve. Where can they leave the tube?
options.why: Completely digested food is made of tiny dissolved pieces. They pass through the wall of the small intestine into the blood, which carries them to all parts of the body.

options.text: It is passed from the small intestine to the stomach.
options.pick: It is easy to mix up the direction that food travels.
options.why: Food moves one way only: stomach, then small intestine, then large intestine. It never goes back to the stomach.

options.text: It is passed from the small intestine to the large intestine.
options.pick: This is true for undigested food such as fibre, so it sounds familiar.
options.why: Only undigested food passes on to the large intestine. Completely digested food was absorbed into the blood before it could get there.

title: The sweetcorn skin
stem:
Mei Ling ate sweetcorn. The tough skin of the corn could not be digested.

Which shows the path taken by the corn skin?
key: Undigested food follows the whole tube: mouth → gullet → stomach → small intestine → large intestine. It never enters the blood.

options.text: mouth → stomach → gullet → small intestine → large intestine
options.pick: It lists all the right parts, so it is easy to pick without checking the order.
options.why: The gullet comes before the stomach. Swallowed food goes down the gullet first.

options.text: mouth → gullet → stomach → small intestine → blood
options.pick: Food ends up in the blood, so this looks like where all food goes.
options.why: Only digested food passes into the blood. The skin cannot be digested, so it cannot pass into the blood.

options.text: mouth → gullet → stomach → large intestine → small intestine
options.pick: The large intestine sounds like it should come first because it is the wider tube.
options.why: Food always goes from the small intestine to the large intestine, never the other way round.

options.text: mouth → gullet → stomach → small intestine → large intestine
options.pick: Check the order part by part, and remember that undigested food cannot enter the blood.
options.why: The skin passes through the small intestine without being absorbed. In the large intestine, water is taken out and what is left becomes faeces.

title: Where digested food enters the blood
stem: In which part of the digestive system does digested food pass into the blood?
key: Digestion is completed in the small intestine, and digested food passes through its wall into the blood.

options.text: Stomach
options.pick: The stomach does a lot of digesting, so it seems to finish the job.
options.why: The stomach only partly digests the food. The food is not yet small enough to pass into the blood there.

options.text: Small intestine
options.pick: Find the part where digestion is completed.
options.why: Digestion is completed in the small intestine, and the tiny dissolved pieces pass through its wall into the blood.

options.text: Large intestine
options.pick: The large intestine absorbs things, so it seems to absorb the food too.
options.why: The large intestine absorbs water from undigested food. Digested food was already absorbed in the small intestine.

options.text: Gullet
options.pick: Food passes through the gullet, so it seems it could be absorbed there.
options.why: The gullet only pushes food down to the stomach. The food has not been digested yet.

title: Inside the large intestine
stem: Which of these happens in the large intestine?
key: The large intestine absorbs water from undigested food. What is left becomes faeces.

options.text: Digested food passes into the blood.
options.pick: The intestines are where food passes into the blood, so this seems right.
options.why: Digested food passes into the blood in the small intestine. None reaches the large intestine.

options.text: Muscles churn the food with gastric juice.
options.pick: Churning sounds like something a large organ would do.
options.why: Churning with gastric juice happens in the stomach.

options.text: Water is absorbed from the undigested food.
options.pick: Only undigested food reaches the large intestine. What is taken out of it there?
options.why: The large intestine absorbs water from the undigested food, and what is left becomes faeces.

options.text: Fibre is digested into tiny pieces.
options.pick: The large intestine is the last stop, so it seems to deal with what was left.
options.why: Fibre cannot be digested anywhere. It leaves the body as part of the faeces.

title: The order of the parts
stem:
Four parts of the digestive system are labelled P, Q, R and S.

In which order does food pass through them?
figure:
LabelPart
Pstomach
Qsmall intestine
Rgullet
Slarge intestine
key: Mouth → gullet → stomach → small intestine → large intestine. Food never goes backwards.

options.text: P → R → Q → S
options.pick: The stomach is the best-known part, so it seems to come first.
options.why: Swallowed food goes down the gullet before it reaches the stomach.

options.text: R → P → S → Q
options.pick: The large intestine is wider, so it seems to come before the small one.
options.why: Food goes from the small intestine to the large intestine, never the other way.

options.text: R → Q → P → S
options.pick: The two intestine-like tubes seem to belong on either side of the stomach.
options.why: The stomach comes straight after the gullet. The small intestine comes after the stomach.

options.text: R → P → Q → S
options.pick: Start from the mouth: the gullet comes first, then the stomach, then the small and large intestines.
options.why: Gullet (R), stomach (P), small intestine (Q), large intestine (S).

title: Fibre from vegetables
stem:
Jun Kai eats rice and vegetables. The fibre in the vegetables cannot be digested.

What happens to the fibre after it leaves the small intestine?
key: Undigested food moves on to the large intestine, where water is absorbed from it, and leaves the body as faeces.

options.text: It passes into the blood.
options.pick: All food seems to end up in the blood eventually.
options.why: Only digested food passes into the blood. Fibre cannot be digested.

options.text: It enters the large intestine, where water is absorbed from it, and leaves the body as part of the faeces.
options.pick: Fibre cannot be digested, so it cannot pass into the blood. Where does it go next?
options.why: Undigested fibre moves on to the large intestine. Water is absorbed from it, and what is left leaves the body as faeces.

options.text: It goes back to the stomach to be digested again.
options.pick: The stomach digests food, so it seems to get a second try.
options.why: Food moves one way only. Nothing goes back to the stomach.

options.text: It enters the large intestine, where it is finally digested.
options.pick: The large intestine is the last stop, so it seems to finish the job.
options.why: Fibre is never digested. Water is absorbed from it in the large intestine, but the fibre itself leaves the body.

title: About the stomach
stem: Which statement about the stomach is correct?
key: The stomach churns food and partly digests it with gastric juice. It does not finish digestion.

options.text: It only stores the food. No digestion happens there.
options.pick: The stomach looks like a bag, so it seems only to hold food.
options.why: Gastric juice in the stomach digests the food. The stomach does more than store it.

options.text: It completes digestion and absorbs the digested food.
options.pick: The stomach is a big organ, so it seems to do the whole job.
options.why: Digestion is completed, and digested food is absorbed, in the small intestine.

options.text: Its muscles churn the food while gastric juice partly digests it.
options.pick: The stomach has a muscular wall and makes gastric juice.
options.why: The muscles churn the food and gastric juice digests it into a thick liquid. Digestion is completed later, in the small intestine.

options.text: It cuts the food into small pieces.
options.pick: Food is broken down there, which sounds like cutting.
options.why: Teeth in the mouth cut the food. The stomach churns it.

title: Pushing food down
stem: Which part of the digestive system pushes food down to the stomach?
key: The gullet is a muscular tube. Its muscles squeeze the food down to the stomach.

options.text: Mouth
options.pick: The tongue pushes food to the back of the mouth, so the mouth seems to do it.
options.why: The tongue pushes food to the back of the mouth to be swallowed. After that, the gullet pushes it down.

options.text: Small intestine
options.pick: The small intestine is a long tube, so it seems to move food along.
options.why: The small intestine comes after the stomach, so it cannot push food down to it.

options.text: Large intestine
options.pick: It is a large tube, so it seems strong enough to push food.
options.why: The large intestine is near the end of the system, after the stomach and the small intestine.

options.text: Gullet
options.pick: Find the tube that joins the mouth to the stomach.
options.why: Muscles in the gullet wall squeeze in waves and push the food down to the stomach.

title: Why only digested food enters the blood
stem: Why can digested food pass into the blood when undigested food cannot?
key: Digested food is broken into tiny pieces that dissolve, so they can pass through the wall of the small intestine.

options.text: Digested food is broken into tiny pieces that dissolve and can pass through the wall of the small intestine.
options.pick: Think about the size of the pieces after digestion.
options.why: Digestion breaks food into tiny pieces that dissolve. Only these can pass through the wall of the small intestine into the blood.

options.text: Undigested food passes into the blood in the large intestine instead.
options.pick: Undigested food goes to the large intestine, so it seems to be absorbed there.
options.why: Undigested food never passes into the blood. Only water is absorbed from it in the large intestine.

options.text: Digested food passes into the blood in the stomach, before undigested food gets there.
options.pick: The stomach digests food, so it seems to send it into the blood.
options.why: Food is only partly digested in the stomach. Digested food passes into the blood in the small intestine.

options.text: Digested food is absorbed in the large intestine together with water.
options.pick: The large intestine absorbs things, so it seems to absorb food too.
options.why: Digested food has already been absorbed in the small intestine. Only water is absorbed in the large intestine.

title: Where water is absorbed
stem: In which part of the digestive system is water absorbed from undigested food?
key: Water is absorbed from undigested food in the large intestine.

options.text: Small intestine
options.pick: The small intestine absorbs digested food, so it seems to absorb water too.
options.why: The small intestine absorbs digested food. Water is taken out of the undigested food later, in the large intestine.

options.text: Large intestine
options.pick: Find the part that receives the undigested food.
options.why: Undigested food arrives in the large intestine as a watery mixture, and water is absorbed from it there.

options.text: Stomach
options.pick: The stomach holds a lot of liquid, so it seems to take the water out.
options.why: The stomach churns food into a thick liquid. Water is absorbed from undigested food in the large intestine.

options.text: Gullet
options.pick: Drinks pass down the gullet, so it seems to absorb water.
options.why: The gullet only moves food and drink down to the stomach.

title: Watery faeces
stem:
A boy's faeces are very watery.

Which part of his digestive system is most likely not doing its job well?
key: The large intestine absorbs water from undigested food. If it does not, the faeces stay watery.

options.text: Stomach
options.pick: The stomach turns food into a liquid, so it seems to be the cause.
options.why: The stomach does make food into a thick liquid, but water is absorbed later, in the large intestine.

options.text: Small intestine
options.pick: The small intestine absorbs things into the blood, so it seems responsible.
options.why: The small intestine absorbs digested food. Water is absorbed from undigested food in the large intestine.

options.text: Large intestine
options.pick: Which part takes water out of the waste before it leaves the body?
options.why: The large intestine absorbs water from undigested food. If too little water is absorbed, the faeces are watery.

options.text: Gullet
options.pick: The gullet is where swallowed drinks go, so it seems linked to water.
options.why: The gullet only pushes food and drink down to the stomach. It plays no part in how watery the faeces are.
